description:
Location: crate-jmap-base-client/src/client.rs:551-574 (connect_ws_session)
          crate-jmap-base-client/src/ws/mod.rs:310-399 (connect_ws / connect_ws_with_limit)

BACKGROUND
JmapClient::connect_ws_session accepts an Option<(&str, &str)> auth_header
parameter. It is wired through to tokio_tungstenite's
`into_client_request` and `HeaderValue::from_str`. If the value fails
header validation, the underlying tungstenite InvalidHeaderValue error is
constructed at ws/mod.rs:363-365.

CONCERN
Two issues, both P3:

1. The connect_ws_session docstring (client.rs:551-574) does NOT warn
   that auth_header is the credential and must not be logged by callers.
   The trait-level AuthProvider doc (auth.rs:100-101) does carry that
   rule, but connect_ws_session takes its own bare tuple — a caller
   reading just the connect_ws_session signature wouldn't see the
   trait-level warning.

2. The InvalidHeaderValue path at ws/mod.rs:363-365 maps the inner
   tungstenite error to:
     ClientError::InvalidArgument("invalid auth header value".to_owned())
   That's good — the original credential bytes are NOT included in the
   error message. But the inner-name path at ws/mod.rs:360-362 maps
   to:
     ClientError::InvalidArgument(format!("invalid auth header name: {e}"))
   The header NAME is interpolated via the http::InvalidHeaderName
   Display, which (per the http crate) does NOT include the
   offending byte sequence verbatim — but a future http-crate version
   could change that. The name path is symmetric to the value path
   for risk; recommend the same string-constant treatment for
   defense-in-depth.

PROPOSED FIX (two changes)
(a) Add a line to connect_ws_session and connect_ws_with_limit
    docstrings:
      /// The `auth_header` value is a credential and must not be
      /// logged or echoed back to other systems. Treat it with the
      /// same care as a BearerAuth token.

(b) Change ws/mod.rs:360-362 from
      `format!("invalid auth header name: {e}")`
    to
      `"invalid auth header name".to_owned()`
    matching the value-path treatment. Loses some diagnostic but
    eliminates any future risk that the http crate begins surfacing
    bytes through its Display impl.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P3 (hygiene / defense-in-depth). The http crate does not currently
leak bytes via either Display impl; this is a tripwire against
upstream behaviour change.

ORACLE
http crate documentation: InvalidHeaderName Display contract.
title: Security: connect_ws_session and connect_ws_with_limit docstrings omit warning that auth_header values may surface in transport error messages
